details: Iran has launched ballistic missiles and drones at Kuwait and Bahrain, hours after the United States and Iran exchanged strikes over the Gulf. This escalation follows the US military shooting down Iranian drones and targeting coastal radar sites. Air raid sirens were reported in Bahrain, and Kuwait's military intercepted drones and missiles. The latest confrontations are straining a tenuous ceasefire and hindering efforts to achieve a permanent peace deal, causing regional instability and disrupting the global economy.
title: Iran Targets Gulf States After US Exchange of Fire, Threatening Fragile Ceasefire

details: Iran is experiencing severe economic challenges, including hyperinflation (food inflation reaching 130%), a 10% economic contraction, and widespread power cuts. The nation is contemplating a shift from wartime unity to a potentially fractious peace. These internal struggles are exacerbated by ongoing US sanctions and a naval blockade that has significantly impacted oil revenues. Discussions within the Iranian regime are emerging regarding the country's post-war future and the potential for lifting economic restrictions.
title: Hyperinflation and Dissent Plague Iran as it Considers Prospects of Peace

details: The US Treasury has imposed new sanctions on Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Nobitex, along with Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex, targeting their senior figures. These measures aim to disrupt Iran's ability to use digital assets to bypass international sanctions. Nobitex reportedly processed over half of all Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025 and facilitated transactions for sanctioned entities, including the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. This action underscores the US's ongoing "maximum pressure" campaign against Tehran's financial networks.
title: US Sanctions Iran's Major Crypto Exchanges to Counter Sanctions Evasion

details: Bitcoin's price has dipped significantly in recent days, falling below the $70,000 mark and even touching $61,500 at one point, with substantial liquidations across the crypto market. This downturn is largely attributed to escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly the US-Iran conflict, which has prompted investors to adopt a "risk-off" approach. Additionally, weakening institutional inflows and sustained outflows from spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have contributed to the selling pressure.
sourceName: News.az (also reported by Investing.com ZA, The Economic Times, Crypto Briefing)
title: Bitcoin Falls Below $70,000 Amid Geopolitical Instability and ETF Outflows
